section: Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation
subsections: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate
Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists

accepted.s: The criteria for identifying the creamy layer among OBCs were framed through which of the following instruments and period?
o: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, based on the Kalelkar Commission
The Ministry of Social Justice notification of 2004, based on the Justice G. Rohini Commission
The DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee
The DoPT Office Memorandum of 2017, based on the Mandal Commission
accepted.x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct instrument, year and associated committee together.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a status-based category associated with exclusion from the OBC creamy layer?
o: Children of senior government and armed-forces officers
Children of constitutional post-holders
Children of all persons belonging to Scheduled Castes
Children of large property owners
accepted.x: Status-based exclusions include children of constitutional post-holders, senior government and armed-forces officers, and specified property owners. Automatic exclusion of all children of Scheduled Castes is not one of the listed criteria.
accepted.tq: Find the option that introduces a category outside the specified status-based exclusions.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the OBC creamy-layer income ceiling:
1. 1993 — ₹1 lakh
2. 2004 — ₹2.5 lakh
3. 2008 — ₹4.5 lakh
4. 2013 — ₹6 lakh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The income ceiling rose from ₹1 lakh in 1993 to ₹2.5 lakh in 2004, ₹4.5 lakh in 2008 and ₹6 lakh in 2013.
accepted.tq: Verify each year-value pair rather than relying on the overall trend.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: The income ceiling for determining the OBC creamy layer, after the 2017 revision and described as still current, is
o: ₹8 lakh per annum
₹4.5 lakh per annum
₹10 lakh per annum
₹6 lakh per annum
accepted.x: The income ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the latest threshold from earlier figures in the revision sequence.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the application of the central creamy-layer threshold in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh applies the threshold only to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Andhra Pradesh has rejected the central threshold for all public-sector definitions.
Andhra Pradesh has fixed a separate threshold of ₹6 lakh for public-sector definitions.
Andhra Pradesh has aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central threshold.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central creamy-layer threshold of ₹8 lakh.
accepted.tq: Test the State-level application of a central numerical standard.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s:
With reference to Union of India v. Rohith Nathan, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court held that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer.
2. The Court ordered the creation of supernumerary posts.
3. In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification concerning 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The 11 March 2026 verdict held that parental salary alone cannot determine creamy-layer status and ordered supernumerary posts. In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification regarding 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
accepted.tq: Combine the judicial holding, consequential direction and subsequent administrative development.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: The Supreme Court decision in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan was delivered on
o: 31 July 2023
11 March 2026
26 August 2026
11 March 2025
accepted.x: The decision in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan was delivered on 11 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of the judgment from dates of later developments and other commissions.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: Who supported the introduction of a creamy-layer principle for Scheduled Castes in the debate mentioned in the context of 2025?
o: The Chief Justice of India, B.R. Gavai
The Chairman of the Kalelkar Commission
The Chairperson of the NCBC
The Union Minister of Social Justice
accepted.x: Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai supported the idea of applying a creamy-layer principle to Scheduled Castes.
accepted.tq: Match the public position with the correct constitutional functionary.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: The Union Government opposed applying the creamy-layer principle to SCs and STs on the ground that their status flows from
o: Articles 341 and 342
Articles 330 and 332
Articles 338B and 342A
Articles 15 and 16
accepted.x: In August 2026, the Union Government opposed the proposal, stating that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional provisions concerning reservations and community identification.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: The creamy-layer principle for OBCs, which excludes socially advanced sections from reservation benefits, was introduced through the decision in
o: Union of India v. Rohith Nathan
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
Indra Sawhney
Jaishri Patil
accepted.x: The creamy-layer principle for excluding socially advanced OBCs was introduced through the Indra Sawhney decision.
accepted.tq: Use the landmark-case association rather than the later constitutional amendment association.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the categories associated with the OBC creamy layer under the Indra Sawhney framework?
o: Children of Class-I officers
All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status
Children whose parents are both Class-II officers
Children of constitutional post-holders
accepted.x: The framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, including children of Class-I officers and parents who are both Class-II officers. It does not exclude all OBC children irrespective of their circumstances.
accepted.tq: Reject the sweeping option that converts specified exclusions into a universal exclusion.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice G. Rohini Commission:
1. It was constituted in October 2017.
2. It received 14 extensions.
3. It was concerned with sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes.
4. Its report was submitted to the President on 31 July 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in October 2017, received 14 extensions, examined sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes, and submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023.
accepted.tq: Check the complete chronology and mandate of the commission statement by statement.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: Which of the following findings was associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 97% of OBC benefits were taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities had zero representation.
The Commission found that only 100 Central-list OBC communities required sub-categorisation.
About 25% of benefits went to 97% of the sub-castes, while no community lacked representation.
All Central-list OBC castes received an equal share of benefits.
accepted.x: The Commission found that approximately 97% of benefits had been taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while around 1,000 communities had zero representation.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversed percentages and population groups in a comparison-based finding.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: The Justice G. Rohini Commission is associated with a proposal to divide the Central-list OBCs into
o: five or six sub-groups
two or three sub-groups
four or five sub-groups
three or four sub-groups
accepted.x: The proposal associated with the Commission envisaged three to four sub-groups among the Central-list OBCs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the proposed range from nearby numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 102nd Constitutional Amendment from the 105th Constitutional Amendment?
o: The 102nd introduced EWS reservation, while the 105th abolished Article 342A.
The 102nd created constitutional status for the NCBC and inserted Article 342A, while the 105th restored States’ power to identify and list SEBCs.
The 102nd restored State power over SEBC lists, while the 105th created the NCBC.
The 102nd created the first Backward Classes Commission, while the 105th repealed the NCBC Act, 1993.
accepted.x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States to identify and list SEBCs.
accepted.tq: Separate the institutional change made by the 102nd Amendment from the federal-list change made by the 105th.
accepted.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional NCBC?
o: It is appointed by State Governors and exercises the powers of a tribunal.
It is appointed by the President and possesses powers of a civil court.
It is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and possesses criminal-court powers.
It is appointed by the Prime Minister and functions only as an advisory body without legal powers.
accepted.x: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the constitutional NCBC are appointed by the President, and the Commission has civil-court powers.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints and what powers’ test to avoid authority and function swaps.
accepted.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed as the Chairperson of the
o: National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Justice G. Rohini Commission
National Commission for Backward Classes
First Backward Classes Commission
accepted.x: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes.
accepted.tq: Match the named person with the correct commission rather than a similarly related body.
accepted.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the statutory NCBC under the 1993 Act with the present constitutional NCBC?
o: The statutory NCBC was constitutional, whereas the present NCBC is merely advisory and statutory.
The statutory NCBC had five members headed by a judge, whereas the constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members.
The statutory NCBC had three members headed by the President, whereas the constitutional NCBC has five judges.
Both bodies had identical composition and powers, but differed only in their names.
accepted.x: The 1993 statutory NCBC had five members and was headed by a judge. The present constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members.
accepted.tq: Compare composition and institutional status instead of focusing only on the common acronym.
accepted.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First Backward Classes Commission under Kalelkar
B. Creation of the statutory NCBC
C. Constitutional status to the NCBC through the 102nd Amendment
D. Restoration of State power over SEBC lists through the 105th Amendment
o: A, B, C, D
B, A, C, D
A, C, B, D
A, B, D, C
accepted.x: The Kalelkar Commission was established in 1953, the statutory NCBC was created in 1993, constitutional status came through the 102nd Amendment in 2018, and State power was restored by the 105th Amendment in 2021.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two NCBC developments between them.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The first Backward Classes Commission in India was the
o: R.N. Prasad Committee
Rohini Commission
Kalelkar Commission
Mandal Commission
accepted.x: The first Backward Classes Commission was the Kalelkar Commission, constituted in 1953.
accepted.tq: Use the first-in-sequence clue to distinguish the foundational commission from later bodies.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following issues has been identified as a criticism or debate concerning reservation in central services?
o: Approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts lie vacant.
All reserved central posts are filled before unreserved posts.
Reserved posts are filled exclusively through State-level commissions.
No reservation is available in central services.
accepted.x: A criticism noted in the reservation debate is that approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts remain vacant.
accepted.tq: Select the stated range while rejecting absolute claims about reservation administration.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The 2027 Census has been discussed as potentially useful for
o: replacing Articles 341 and 342
determining the composition of the NCBC by direct election
abolishing all OBC lists
reassessing reservation quotas using caste enumeration
accepted.x: The 2027 Census, with caste enumeration, may be used to reassess reservation quotas.
accepted.tq: Link the proposed data exercise to its stated policy application without extending its purpose.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following represents a reservation-related issue specifically associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: The creation of the constitutional NCBC by the State Legislature
The replacement of the Central List by a district-wise list
BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand
The demand to abolish all BC-A to BC-E groups
accepted.x: BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand are identified as live reservation issues in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Separate State-specific reservation issues from national constitutional developments.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh Social Welfare and Education Society residential school admissions for 2024–25, BC admissions continue to be organised through
o: only a single undivided BC category, with BC-E having 10 per cent
the Central List alone, without any State grouping
BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E having 4 per cent
four groups from BC-A to BC-D, with no BC-E category
accepted.x: APSES residential school admissions for 2024–25 continue to use BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E carrying 4 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the category range and the associated percentage together.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following developments relates to the reservation debate in 2026?
o: The Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to include a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.
The Supreme Court directed that no caste enumeration could be considered in Census 2027.
The Union Government abolished the BC/OBC category in the Census.
The Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to remove caste-related questions from Census 2027.
accepted.x: On 12 September 2026, the Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to add a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific institutional demand and distinguish it from an opposite or absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the current debate on reservation for women?
o: Women's reservation has replaced all OBC reservation in central posts.
The NCBC has constitutional authority to impose a BC sub-quota in every State.
A BC sub-quota exists inside women's reservation throughout India.
There is no BC sub-quota inside women's reservation, which has been raised as a criticism.
accepted.x: The absence of a BC sub-quota within women's reservation has been identified as a criticism and debate.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal between an identified criticism and a claim that the arrangement already exists.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Supreme Court’s reserved verdict mentioned in the context of August 2026 concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota for
o: persons converted to Christianity only
persons converted to Islam
all religious communities without distinction
persons converted to Buddhism
accepted.x: The reserved Supreme Court verdict concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota in relation to persons who converted to Islam.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise community and issue rather than broadening the religious category.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
